previous_goal_turn: Progress: recurring command capture was implemented and verified with 148 tests; interpreter and C API removal milestones remain completed.
scope: Port the existing scheduled renderer-property and pending-destination capture needed by production song compilation. Migration acceptance criteria are unchanged.
implementation: Publish ten scheduled render targets through the shared ordered property buffer, retaining delays, duration, easing, explicit writes, duplicate replacement and message provenance. Accept compiler pending render destinations across drains; Stop clears them and Finish merges newer writes before publishing and restoring render state, including the disabled FOV sentinel.

development_runs.explanation: All existing selected checks passed. New fixture assumptions failed: canonical accelerate easing is inQuad; queueing inside the message did not fail synchronously. Retained exact native/Rust comparisons, corrected the canonical-label assertion, and used explicit PlayCommand to test synchronous error propagation.

Added pending destination handoff. Review then found that restoring old pending getters after newer same-frame writes could leave stale render state. Fixed merge order and added native getter comparisons plus Stop/FOV-sentinel assertions.

limits: The scheduled render family covers ZBias, DrawOrder, DrawByZPosition, Fov, Vanishpoint, Blend, DepthTest, DepthTestOnFail, DepthWrite and TextureFiltering. These comparisons use captured commands without future frame-clock prediction. The new route does not yet supply future queue progress or cross-actor frame-advance prediction. Remaining text/sprite channels and complete production compiler/live orchestration still require migration.
remaining: Complete queue-clock prediction/dynamic recurrence, remaining scheduled pose/text/media capture, full overlay extraction and tracked/wrapper remapping, compiler/live sessions and fallback/cache, unconditional production cutover, then all original fixture/application/render/dependency/link/performance gates.
